html:
A Nigerian musician and activist who created Afrobeat and used it to attack military rule and corruption. His mother, Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti, was a leading campaigner for women's rights.

He studied music in London, then mixed West African highlife, jazz, American funk and Yoruba rhythms into long, hypnotic songs, sung in Pidgin English so that ordinary people across West Africa could follow. His band Africa 70, with the drummer Tony Allen, made the sound famous.

In Lagos he declared his compound the Kalakuta Republic, independent of the state. After his album Zombie mocked soldiers as mindless, about a thousand troops stormed the compound in February 1977, during the FESTAC 77 festival. They beat him, burned the house, and threw his elderly mother from a window; she died of her injuries. He was jailed again in 1984.

He died in 1997 of an illness related to AIDS. Huge crowds attended his funeral. His sons Femi and Seun carry on his music.
sum: A Nigerian musician and activist who created Afrobeat and used it to attack military rule and corruption. His mother, Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti, was a leading campaigner for women's rights.
